en: Ever since the beginning of computing, many high-valued applications have demanded more execution speed and resources than the computing devices can offer. Early applications relied on the advancement of processor speed, memory speed, and memory capacity to enhance application-level capabilities such as the timeliness of weather forecast, the accuracy of engineering structural analysis, the realism of computer-generated graphics, the number of airline reservations processed per second, or the number of fund transfers processed per second. More recently, new applications such as deep learning have demanded even more execution speed and resources than what the best computing devices can offer. These application demands have fueled fast advancement in computing device capabilities in the past five decades and will continue to do so in the foreseeable future.

Microprocessors based on a single central processing unit (CPU) that appear to execute instructions in sequential steps, such as those in the x86 processors from Intel and AMD, armed with fast increasing clock frequency and hardware resources, drove rapid performance increases and cost reductions in computer applications in the 1980s and 1990s. During these two decades of growth, single-CPU microprocessors brought GFLOPS, or giga (10^9) floating-point operations per second, to desktop computers and TFLOPS, or tera (10^12) floating-point operations per second, to datacenters. This relentless drive for performance improvement has allowed application software to provide more functionality, have better user interfaces, and generate more useful results. The users, in turn, demand even more improvements once they become accustomed to these improvements, creating a positive (virtuous) cycle for the computer industry.

This drive, however, slowed down since 2003 due to energy consumption and heat dissipation issues. These issues limited the increase of the clock frequency, the productive activities that could be performed in each clock period within a single CPU while maintaining the appearance of executing instructions in sequential steps. Since then, virtually all microprocessor vendors switched to a model where multiple physical CPUs, referred to as processor cores, are used in each chip to increase its processing power. A traditional CPU can be viewed as a single-core processor in this model. In order to benefit from the multiple processor cores, users must run multiple instruction sequences, whether from the same application or different applications, that can simultaneously execute on these processor cores. For a particular application to benefit from multiple processor cores, its work must be divided into multiple instruction sequences that can simultaneously execute on these processor cores. This switch from a single CPU executing instructions in sequential steps to multiple cores executing multiple instruction sequences in parallel had a tremendous impact on the software developer community.

Traditionally, the vast majority of software applications were written as sequential programs that were executed by processors whose design was envisioned by von Neumann in his seminal report in 1945 [1]. The execution of these programs can be understood by a human as sequentially stepping through the program code based on the concept of a program counter, also known as an instruction pointer in the literature. The program counter contains the memory address of the next instruction that will be executed by the processor. The sequence of instruction execution activities resulting from this sequential stepwise execution of an application is referred to as a thread of execution, or simply a thread, in the literature. The concept of thread is so important that it will be more formally defined and used extensively in this book.

Historically, most software developers relied on the advances in hardware, such as increased clock speed and executing multiple instructions under the hood, to increase the speed of their sequential applications; the same software simply ran faster as each new processor generation was introduced. Computer users were also accustomed to the expectation that these programs ran faster with each new generation of microprocessors. This expectation has not been valid for over a decade. A sequential program only runs on one of the processor cores, which is no longer becoming significantly faster from generation to generation. Without performance improvements, sequential application developers were no longer able to introduce new features and capabilities into their software as new microprocessors were introduced, reducing the growth opportunities of the entire computer industry.

Rather, the application software that continued to enjoy significant performance improvement with each new generation of microprocessors was parallel software, in which multiple threads of execution cooperate to complete the work faster. The dramatically escalated advantage of parallel programs over sequential programs is referred to as the concurrency revolution [2]. The practice of parallel programming was by no means new. The high-performance computing community had been developing parallel programs for decades. These parallel programs typically ran on large-scale, expensive computers. Only a few elite applications could justify the use of these expensive computers, thus limiting the practice of parallel programming to a small number of application developers. However, when all microprocessors became parallel computers, the number of applications that needed to be developed as parallel programs increased dramatically. There is a greater need for software developers to learn about parallel programming, which is the focus of this book.

Data parallelism refers to the phenomenon that the computations to be performed on different parts of a dataset can be done independently of each other and thus can be done in parallel with each other. Many applications exhibit a rich amount of data parallelism that makes them amenable to scalable parallel execution where the speed of execution improves proportionally to the amount of execution resources in the system. It is therefore important for parallel programmers to be familiar with the concept of data parallelism and the parallel programming language constructs for writing code that exploit data parallelism. In this chapter, we will use the CUDA C++ language constructs to develop a simple data parallel program.
zh: 所谓数据并行性（data parallelism），是指对数据集不同部分要执行的计算彼此独立、因而可以与彼此并行执行这一现象。许多应用都表现出丰富的数据并行性，使它们非常适合可扩展的并行执行——执行速度随系统中执行资源的数量成比例提升。因此，并行程序员熟悉数据并行性的概念，以及用于编写利用数据并行性的代码的并行编程语言构造，就显得尤为重要。在本章中，我们将使用 CUDA C++ 语言构造来实现一个简单的数据并行程序。

en: In Chapter 2, we learned to write a simple CUDA C++ program that calls a kernel function to launch a one-dimensional grid of threads that operates on elements of one-dimensional arrays. A kernel specifies the statements that are executed by each individual thread in the grid. In this chapter, we look more generally at how threads are organized and learn how threads and blocks can be used to process multidimensional arrays. Multiple examples are used throughout the chapter, including converting a colored image to a grayscale image, blurring an image, and matrix multiplication. These examples also serve to familiarize the reader with reasoning about data parallelism before we proceed to discuss the GPU architecture, memory organization, and performance optimizations in the upcoming chapters.
zh: 在第 2 章中，我们学会了编写一个简单的 CUDA C++ 程序：它调用一个内核函数，启动由一维网格线程组成的程序来处理一维数组的元素。内核规定了网格中每个线程所执行的语句。在本章中，我们将更一般地考察线程的组织方式，学习如何利用线程和线程块来处理多维数组。本章通篇使用多个例子，包括把彩色图像转换为灰度图像、图像模糊以及矩阵乘法。这些例子还将帮助读者建立对数据并行性的推理能力，为后续章节讨论 GPU 架构、内存组织与性能优化做好准备。

en: In Chapter 1, we saw that CPUs are designed to minimize the latency of instruction execution and that GPUs are designed to maximize the throughput of executing instructions. In Chapter 2 and Chapter 3, we learned the core features of CUDA programming for creating and calling kernels to launch and execute threads. In the next three chapters, we discuss the architecture of modern GPUs, both the compute architecture and the memory architecture, and the performance optimization techniques stemming from the understanding of this architecture.

This chapter presents several aspects of the GPU compute architecture that are essential for CUDA C++ programmers to understand and reason about the performance behavior of their kernel code. We start by showing a high-level simplified view of the compute architecture and explore the concepts of flexible resource assignment, scheduling of thread blocks, and occupancy. We then advance into thread scheduling, latency tolerance, control divergence, and synchronization. We will finish the chapter with a description of the API functions that can be used to query the resources available in the GPU and the tools to help estimate the occupancy of the GPU when executing a kernel.

In the following two chapters, we present the core concepts and programming considerations of the GPU memory architecture. In particular, Chapter 5 focuses on the on-chip memory architecture, and Chapter 6 briefly covers the off-chip memory architecture then elaborates on various performance considerations of the GPU architecture as a whole. A CUDA C++ programmer who masters these concepts is well equipped to write and to understand high-performance parallel kernels.
zh: 在第 1 章中，我们看到 CPU 的设计目标是尽量降低指令执行延迟，而 GPU 的设计目标是尽量提高指令执行吞吐量。在第 2 章和第 3 章中，我们学习了 CUDA 编程的核心特性，能够创建并调用内核来启动和执行线程。在接下来的三章里，我们讨论现代 GPU 的架构——包括计算架构和内存架构——以及建立在这种理解之上的性能优化技术。
本章介绍 GPU 计算架构的若干方面，CUDA C++ 程序员必须理解这些方面，才能对其内核代码的性能表现进行推理。我们先给出计算架构的高层简化视图，探讨灵活的资源分配、线程块调度与占用率（occupancy）等概念；然后进一步讨论线程调度、延迟容忍、控制流分歧与同步；最后，本章介绍可用于查询 GPU 中可用资源的 API 函数，以及帮助估算内核执行时 GPU 占用率的工具。
在随后的两章中，我们介绍 GPU 内存架构的核心概念与编程考量。特别地，第 5 章聚焦片上内存架构；第 6 章先简要介绍片外内存架构，随后详细讨论 GPU 整体架构的各种性能考量。掌握了这些概念的 CUDA C++ 程序员，就能胜任编写和理解高性能并行内核的工作。

en: So Far, we have learned how to write a CUDA kernel function and how to configure and coordinate its execution by a massive number of threads. We have also looked at the compute architecture of GPU hardware and how threads are scheduled to execute. In this chapter, we will focus on the on-chip memory architecture of the GPU and begin to study how one can organize and position data for efficient access by a massive number of threads. The CUDA kernels that we have learned so far will likely achieve only a tiny fraction of the potential speed of the underlying hardware. This poor performance is because global memory, which is typically implemented with off-chip DRAM, tends to have long access latency (hundreds of clock cycles) and finite access bandwidth. While having many threads available for execution can theoretically tolerate long memory-access latencies, one can easily run into a situation where traffic congestion in the global memory access paths prevents all but very few threads from making progress, thus rendering some of the cores in the Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) idle. To circumvent such congestion, GPUs provide a number of additional on-chip memory resources for accessing data that can remove the majority of redundant traffic to and from the global memory. In this chapter, we study the use of different memory types to boost the execution performance of CUDA kernels.
zh: 到目前为止，我们学会了如何编写 CUDA 内核函数，以及如何配置和协调由海量线程执行的程序。我们还了解了 GPU 硬件的计算架构，以及线程如何被调度执行。在本章中，我们将聚焦 GPU 的片上内存架构，开始研究如何组织和放置数据，才能被海量线程高效访问。到目前为止我们学过的 CUDA 内核，很可能只能发挥底层硬件潜在速度的一小部分。这种糟糕性能的原因在于全局内存：全局内存通常用片外 DRAM 实现，访问延迟长（数百个时钟周期），访问带宽也有限。虽然拥有大量可执行线程理论上可以容忍长的内存访问延迟，但实际很容易遇到这样一种情况：全局内存访问路径上的交通拥塞使几乎没有什么线程能向前推进，从而导致流式多处理器（SM）中的部分处理器空闲。为了避开这种拥塞，GPU 提供了多种额外的片上内存资源，借助它们访问数据，可以消除全局内存往返流量中的大部分冗余流量。在本章中，我们研究如何使用不同的内存类型来提升 CUDA 内核的执行性能。

en: The execution speed of a parallel program can vary greatly depending on the interactions between the resource demands of the program and the resource constraints of the hardware. Managing the interaction between parallel code and hardware resource constraints is important for achieving high performance in virtually all parallel programming models. It is a practical skill that requires deep understanding of the hardware architecture and is best learned with hands-on exercises in a parallel programming model designed for high-performance.

So far, we have learned about the basic aspects of the GPU architecture and their implications on performance. In Chapter 4, we learned about the compute architecture of the GPU and related performance considerations such as control divergence and occupancy. In Chapter 5, we learned about the on-chip memory architecture of the GPU and the use of shared memory tiling and register tiling to alleviate global memory bandwidth limitations. In this chapter, we will learn more about the off-chip memory (DRAM) architecture and discuss related performance considerations such as memory coalescing, memory latency hiding, and vector loads and stores. We also introduce additional important optimizations such as avoiding shared memory bank conflicts, thread granularity coarsening, loop unrolling, and double-buffering. Finally, we wrap up this part of the textbook with a checklist of common performance optimizations that will serve as a guide for optimizing the performance of the parallel patterns discussed in the second and third parts of the book.

Since different applications impose different demands on architectural resources, different architecture constraints may dominate and become the limiting factors of performance, commonly referred to as bottlenecks. One can often dramatically improve the performance of an application on a particular CUDA device, by trading one resource usage for another. This strategy works well if the resource constraint thus alleviated was the dominating constraint before the strategy was applied and the one thus exacerbated does not have negative effects on parallel execution. Without such understanding, performance tuning would be a guess work; plausible strategies may or may not lead to performance enhancements.
zh: 并行程序的执行速度可以相差很大，这取决于程序对资源的需求与硬件的资源约束之间的相互作用。管理并行代码与硬件资源约束之间的相互作用，对几乎所有并行编程模型实现高性能都很重要。这是一项实践技能，要求对硬件架构有深入理解，并且最好在面向高性能设计的并行编程模型中通过动手练习来掌握。

到目前为止，我们学习了 GPU 架构的基本方面及其对性能的影响。在第 4 章中，我们学习了 GPU 的计算架构，以及控制流分歧、占用率等相关性能考量。在第 5 章中，我们学习了 GPU 的片上内存架构，以及利用共享内存分块和寄存器分块缓解全局内存带宽限制的方法。在本章中，我们将进一步了解片外内存（DRAM）架构，讨论相关的性能考量，如内存合并、内存延迟隐藏以及向量装载与存储。我们还将介绍更多重要优化，例如避免共享内存 bank 冲突、线程粒度粗化、循环展开和双缓冲。最后，我们用一份常见性能优化清单为本部分收尾，作为优化本书第二、三部分所讨论的并行模式性能的指南。
由于不同应用对架构资源的需求不同，起主导作用、成为性能限制因素的架构约束（通常称为瓶颈）也各不相同。通过用一种资源的用量换取另一种资源，人们往往能显著提升某个应用在特定 CUDA 设备上的性能。如果由此缓解的资源约束正是策略应用之前的主导约束，且被加重的约束不会对并行执行产生负面影响，这一策略就会奏效。没有这种理解，性能调优就成了猜测；看似合理的策略也许能，也许不能带来性能提升。

en: In the next several chapters, we discuss a set of important patterns of parallel computation. These patterns are the basis of a wide range of parallel algorithms that appear in many parallel applications. We start with convolution, which is a popular array operation that is used in various forms in signal processing, digital recording, image processing, video processing, and computer vision. In these application areas, convolution is often performed as a filter that transforms signals and pixels into more desirable values. Our image blur kernel is such a filter that smooths out the signal values so that one can see the big-picture trend. For another example, Gaussian filters are convolution filters that can be used to sharpen boundaries and edges of objects in images.

Convolution typically performs a significant number of arithmetic operations to generate each output element. For large data sets, such as high-definition images and videos where there are many output elements (pixels), the amount of computation can be huge. On one hand, the output data elements of the convolution computation can be calculated independently of each other, a desirable trait for parallel computing. On the other hand, there is a substantial amount of input data sharing when processing different output data elements with somewhat challenging boundary conditions. These properties make convolution an important use case for sophisticated tiling methods and input data staging methods, which are the focus of this chapter.
zh: 在接下来的几章中，我们将讨论一组重要的并行计算模式。这些模式是很多并行应用中大量并行算法的基础。我们从卷积开始。卷积是一种流行的数组运算，在信号处理、数字记录、图像处理、视频处理和计算机视觉中以各种形式使用。在这些应用领域，卷积常常作为滤波器执行，把信号和像素变换为更理想的值。我们的图像模糊内核就是这样一种滤波器：它把信号值抹平，使人能看到大趋势。再举一个例子，高斯滤波器是可用于锐化图像中物体边界和边缘的卷积滤波器。
卷积通常为生成每个输出元素要执行大量算术运算。对大规模数据集，例如输出元素（像素）极多的高清图像和视频，计算量可能非常巨大。一方面，卷积计算的输出数据元素彼此可以独立计算，这是并行计算希望看到的特性；另一方面，处理不同输出数据元素时又存在大量的输入数据共享，边界条件也颇为棘手。这些特性使卷积成为精细的分块方法与输入数据摆渡方法的重要用例，而这些正是本章的重点。

en: Stencils are foundational to numerical methods for solving partial differential equations in application domains like fluid dynamics, heat conductance, combustion, weather forecast, climate simulation, and electromagnetics. The data processed by stencil-based algorithms are discretized quantities of physical significance, such as mass, velocity, force, acceleration, temperature, electrical field, and energy whose relations with each other are governed by differential equations. A common use of stencils is to approximate the derivative values of a function based on the function values within a range of input variable values. Stencils bear strong resemblance to convolution in that they both calculate the new value of an element of a multidimensional array based on the current value of the element at the same position and those in the neighborhood in another multidimensional array. Therefore, stencils also need to deal with halo cells and ghost cells. Unlike convolution, a stencil computation is used to iteratively solve the values of continuous and differentiable functions within the domain of interest. The data elements and the weight coefficients used for the elements in the stencil neighborhood are governed by the differential equations being solved. Some stencil patterns are amenable to optimizations that are not applicable to convolution. In the solvers where initial conditions are iteratively propagated through the domain, the calculations of output values may have dependences and need to be performed according to some ordering constraints. Furthermore, because of the numerical accuracy requirements in solving differential equations, the data processed by stencils tend to be high-precision floating data that consume more on-chip memory for tiling techniques. Due to these differences, stencils tend to motivate different optimizations than convolution.
zh: 模板是流体动力学、热传导、燃烧、天气预报、气候模拟和电磁学等应用领域中求解偏微方程数值方法的基础。基于模板的算法所处理的数据是具有物理意义的量的离散化表示，例如质量、速度、力、加速度、温度、电场和能量，它们相互之间的关系由微分方程支配。模板的一个常见用途，是基于自变量取值范围内的函数值来近似函数的导数值。模板与卷积高度相似：二者都是依据同一位置上元素的当前值以及另一个多维数组中邻域元素的当前值，来计算一个多维数组中元素的新值。因此，模板同样要处理边缘单元（halo cell）与虚拟单元（ghost cell）。与卷积不同的是，模板计算用于在感兴趣区域内迭代求解连续可微函数的值。模板及其邻域元素所使用的数据元素和权重系数，都由所求解的微分方程决定。有些模板模式可以采用不适用于卷积的优化。在把初始条件沿区域迭代传播的求解器中，输出值的计算可能存在依赖，需要按某种次序约束执行。此外，由于求解微分方程对数值精度的要求，模板处理的数据往往是高精度浮点数据，分块技术要消耗更多片上内存。由于这些差异，模板往往催生与卷积不同的优化。

en: The parallel computation patterns that we have presented so far all allow the task of computing each output element to be exclusively assigned to, or owned by, a thread. Therefore, these patterns are amenable to the owner-computes rule, where every thread can write into their designated output element(s) without any concern about interference from other threads. This chapter introduces the parallel histogram pattern, where each output element can potentially be updated by any thread. As such, one must take care to coordinate among threads as they update output elements and avoid any interference that corrupts the final result. In practice, there are many other important parallel computation patterns where output interference cannot be easily avoided. The parallel histogram pattern provides an example of such output interference. We will first examine a baseline approach that uses atomic operations to serialize the updates to each element. This baseline approach is simple but inefficient, often resulting in disappointing execution speed. We will then present some widely used optimization techniques, most notably privatization, to significantly enhance execution speed while preserving correctness. The cost and benefit of these techniques depend on the underlying hardware as well as the characteristics of the input data. It is therefore important for a developer to understand the key ideas of these techniques and reason about their applicability under different circumstances.
zh: 我们此前介绍的并行计算模式，都允许把计算每个输出元素的任务专门指派给某个线程（即由它“拥有”）。因此，这些模式都符合“拥有者计算（owner-computes）”规则：每个线程可以写入指定的输出元素，而不必担心其他线程的干扰。本章介绍并行直方图模式：在这种模式中，每个输出元素都可能被任何线程更新。因此，在线程更新输出元素时，必须注意线程之间的协调，避免任何破坏最终结果的干扰。实际上，还有许多其他重要的并行计算模式无法轻易避免输出干扰，并行直方图模式正是这种输出干扰的一个例子。我们先考察一个使用原子操作把对每个元素的更新串行化的基线方法。这个基线方法简单但低效，执行速度常常令人失望。随后我们介绍一些广泛使用的优化技术，最典型的是私有化（privatization），在保持正确性的同时显著提升执行速度。这些技术的代价和收益取决于底层硬件以及输入数据的特征。因此，开发者理解这些技术的关键思想、并能在不同情形下推理其适用性，是非常重要的。

en: A reduction operation derives a single value from a list of values. The single value could be the sum, the maximum, the minimum, etc. of all the values in the list. The value can also be of various types: integer, single-precision floating point, double-precision floating point, half-precision floating point, characters, etc. All these types of reductions share the same computation structure. Like histogram, reduction is an important computation pattern as it generates a summary from a large amount of data. Parallel reduction is an important parallel pattern that requires parallel threads to coordinate with each other to produce correct results. Such coordination must be done carefully to avoid performance bottlenecks commonly found in parallel computing systems. Parallel reduction is therefore a good vehicle for illustrating these performance bottlenecks and introducing techniques for mitigating them.
zh: 归约（reduction）操作从一组数值列表中导出单个值。这个单值可以是所有值的和、最大值、最小值，等等。值的类型也可以多种多样：整数、单精度浮点、双精度浮点、半精度浮点、字符，等等。所有这些类型的归约都共享相同的计算结构。和直方图一样，归约是一种重要的计算模式，因为它从大量数据中生成摘要。并行归约是一种重要的并行模式，它要求并行线程彼此协调才能产生正确结果。这种协调必须小心处理，以避免并行计算系统中常见的性能瓶颈。因此，并行归约是说明这些性能瓶颈、介绍缓解技术的绝佳载体。

en: Parallel scan is frequently used to parallelize seemingly sequential operations, such as resource allocation, work assignment, and polynomial evaluation. In general, if a computation is naturally described as a mathematical recursion where each item in a series is defined in terms of the previous item, it is likely parallelizable as a parallel scan operation. Parallel scan plays a key role in massively parallel computing for a simple reason: any sequential section of an application can drastically limit the overall performance of the application. Many such sequential sections can be converted into parallel computation with parallel scan. For this reason, parallel scan is often used as a primitive operation in parallel algorithms that perform filtering, radix sort, quick sort, string comparison, polynomial evaluation, solving recurrences, and tree operations. The filtering example is presented in Chapter 12 and the radix sort example is presented in Chapter 14.

Multiple algorithms exist for parallel scan with different tradeoffs between work complexity and span. Some parallel algorithms can have higher work complexity than a sequential algorithm. As we shall discuss in this chapter, an increase in work complexity can make a parallel scan run slower than a sequential scan when hardware resources are constrained, necessitating optimizations that mitigate the higher work complexity. We also use parallel scan as an example to introduce new techniques such as double-buffering and unidirectional synchronization, as well as showcase other optimizations that we have already seen such as using warp-level primitives, thread coarsening, and register tiling.
zh: 并行扫描（scan）常被用来将看似顺序的操作并行化，例如资源分配、任务分配和多项式求值。一般而言，如果一个计算可以自然地描述为一种数学递归——序列中每一项都由前一项定义——那么它很可能可以作为并行扫描操作来并行化。并行扫描在大规模并行计算中之所以扮演关键角色，原因很简单：应用的任何顺序片段都可能严重限制应用的整体性能，而许多这样的顺序片段可以借助并行扫描转换为并行计算。因此，并行扫描常被用作执行过滤、基数排序、快速排序、字符串比较、多项式求值、递推求解和树操作的并行算法中的原语操作。过滤示例在第 12 章给出，基数排序示例在第 14 章给出。
存在多种并行扫描算法，它们在工作量（work）复杂度与跨度（span）之间的权衡各不相同。有些并行算法的工作量复杂度可能高于顺序算法。正如本章将讨论的，当硬件资源受限时，工作量复杂度的增加会使并行扫描比重顺序扫描还慢，因而需要能缓解更高工作量复杂度的优化。我们还将以并行扫描为例，介绍双缓冲、单向同步等新技术，并综合展示我们已经见过的其他优化，如使用 warp 级原语、线程粗化和寄存器分块。

en: Filter operations rearrange data in a list to make more efficient use of memory after some of the list elements are deleted. If we view the deleted elements and the remaining elements as two sub-lists, a filter operation can be viewed as the inverse of a merge operation. In this chapter, we show that using a technique called warp voting we can enable coalescing of atomic operations across threads and improve the speed of parallel implementations of filter. We look at the considerations for performing the stable filter operation in place instead of out of place. Finally, we discuss other related patterns with similar implementations and optimizations, such as removing duplicates from a sorted list and adding/removing rows and columns from a matrix.
zh: 过滤（filter）操作在列表中删除某些元素后重新排列数据，以更高效地利用内存。如果我们把被删除的元素和保留的元素看作两个子列表，过滤操作可以看作归并操作的逆运算。在本章中，我们将展示如何利用一种称为 warp 投票（warp voting）的技术，实现跨线程原子操作的合并，提升过滤并行实现的速度。我们还将探讨就地（in place）而非异地（out of place）执行稳定过滤操作的考量。最后，我们讨论其他具有类似实现和优化的相关模式，例如从有序列表中删除重复项，以及从矩阵中添加/删除行和列。

en: Our next parallel pattern is an ordered merge operation, which takes two sorted lists and generates a combined, sorted list. Ordered merge operations can be used as a building block of sorting algorithms as we will see in Chapter 14. Ordered merge operations also form the basis of modern map-reduce frameworks. This chapter presents a parallel ordered merge algorithm where the input data for each thread is dynamically determined. The dynamic nature of the data access makes it challenging to exploit locality and tiling techniques for improved memory access efficiency and performance. The principles behind dynamic input data identification are also relevant to many other important computations, such as set intersection and set union. We present increasingly sophisticated buffer management schemes for achieving increasing levels of memory access efficiency for order merged and other operations that determine their input data dynamically.
zh: 我们的下一个并行模式是有序归并操作：接收两个有序列表，生成一个合并后的有序列表。正如我们将在第 14 章看到的，有序归并操作可以用作排序算法的构件。有序归并操作还构成了现代 map-reduce 框架的基础。本章介绍一种并行有序归并算法，其中每个线程的输入数据是动态确定的。数据访问的这种动态特性，使利用局部性和分块技术来提高内存访问效率和性能变得困难。动态输入数据识别背后的原理，也与许多其他重要计算相关，例如集合交集和集合并集。我们给出渐趋精细的缓冲区管理方案，为有序归并及其他动态确定输入数据的操作实现渐高的内存访问效率。

en: Sorting algorithms place the data elements of a list into a certain order. Sorting is foundational to modern data and information services since the computational complexity of retrieving information from data sets can be significantly reduced if the data set is in proper order. For example, sorting is often used to canonicalize the data for fast comparison and reconciliation between data lists. Also, the efficiency of many data processing algorithms can be improved if the data is in a certain order. Due to their importance, efficient sorting algorithms have been the subject of many computer science research efforts. Even with these efficient algorithms, sorting large data lists is still time consuming and can benefit from parallel execution. Parallelizing efficient sorting algorithms is challenging and sometimes requires elaborate designs. This chapter presents the designs of three parallel sorting algorithms -- odd-even sort, merge sort, and radix sort. Odd-even sort is covered briefly due to its simplicity and merge sort is covered briefly because it largely depends on the merge pattern already presented in Chapter 13. Most of the chapter is dedicated to radix sort and its optimizations, which rely on a more general form of the stable filter pattern which will be discussed further in Chapter 12. Other popular parallel sorting algorithms such as transposition sort and sampling sort are also discussed.
zh: 排序算法把列表的数据元素排列成某种次序。排序是现代数据与信息服务的基石，因为如果数据集处于恰当次序，从数据集中检索信息的计算复杂度可以显著降低。例如，排序常被用来把数据规范化，以便在数据列表之间快速比较和对账。而且，许多数据处理算法在数据处于某种次序时效率更高。由于其重要性，高效排序算法一直是众多计算机科学研究的主题。即使有了这些高效算法，对大数据列表排序仍然耗时，并能从并行执行中获益。将高效排序算法并行化是有挑战的，有时需要精心设计。本章介绍三种并行排序算法的设计——奇偶交换排序、归并排序和基数排序。奇偶交换排序因简单而简略介绍；归并排序因主要依赖第 13 章已介绍的归并模式也简略介绍。本章大部分篇幅献给基数排序及其优化，后者依赖稳定过滤模式的一种更一般形式（第 12 章有更进一步的讨论）。我们还讨论其他流行的并行排序算法，如置换排序和采样排序。

en: Matrix multiplication is an important operation in science, engineering, and graphics applications. Due to its high computation complexity, it exhibits a high degree of data reuse and thus significant optimization opportunities. In Chapter 3, we used matrix multiplication as an example of mapping multi-dimensional grids to data. Subsequently, in Chapter 5, we used matrix multiplication as an example of using shared memory tiling to reduce global memory accesses. In this chapter, we will dive more deeply into matrix multiplication and the advanced optimizations for this important computation on the GPU architecture.
zh: 矩阵乘法是科学、工程和图形应用中的一种重要运算。由于其计算复杂度高，它表现出高度的数据复用，从而存在可观的优化机会。在第 3 章中，我们用矩阵乘法作为把多维网格映射到数据的示例。随后在第 5 章中，我们用矩阵乘法作为利用共享内存分块减少全局内存访问的示例。在本章中，我们将更深入地研究矩阵乘法，以及这种重要计算在 GPU 架构上的高级优化。

en: Wavefront parallelism is an algorithmic technique for exploiting data parallelism in applications with data dependencies along space and/or time dimensions. In this chapter, we study wavefront parallelism in the context of dynamic programming applications. Dynamic programming represents a class of problems that can be solved by dividing a problem into smaller sub-problems. The solution to the original problem can be found by assembling the solutions found for the sub-problems. Parallelizing dynamic programming algorithms on GPUs entails interesting challenges in terms of hardware utilization and synchronization across threads. In this chapter, we discuss these challenges and present software techniques that address them efficiently.
zh: 波纹（wavefront）并行是一种算法技术，用于在沿空间和/或时间维度存在数据依赖的应用中开发数据并行性。在本章中，我们在动态规划应用的背景下研究波纹并行。动态规划代表一类可以通过把问题划分为更小子问题来求解的问题：原问题的解可以通过组装子问题的解来得到。在 GPU 上并行化动态规划算法，在硬件利用率和线程间同步方面带来了有趣的挑战。在本章中，我们讨论这些挑战，并给出高效应对它们的软件技术。

en: Our next parallel pattern is sparse matrix computation. In a sparse matrix, the majority of the elements are zeros. Storing and processing these zero elements are wasteful in terms of memory capacity, memory bandwidth, time, and energy. Many important real-world problems involve sparse matrix computation. Due to the importance of these problems, several sparse matrix storage formats and their corresponding processing methods have been developed and are widely used in the field. All these methods employ some type of compaction techniques to avoid storing or processing zero elements at the cost of introducing some level of irregularity into the data representation. Unfortunately, such irregularity can lead to underutilization of memory bandwidth, control flow divergence, and load imbalance in parallel computing. It is therefore important to strike a good balance between compaction and regularization. Some storage formats achieve a high level of compaction at a high level of irregularity. Others achieve a more moderate level of compaction while keeping the representation more regular. The relative performance of a parallel computation using each storage format is known to be heavily dependent on the distribution of non-zero elements in the sparse matrices. Understanding the wealth of work in sparse matrix storage formats and their corresponding parallel algorithms gives a parallel programmer important background for addressing compaction and regularization challenges in solving related problems.
zh: 我们的下一个并行模式是稀疏矩阵计算。在稀疏矩阵中，大多数元素是零。存储和处理这些零元素，在内存容量、内存带宽、时间和能量上都是浪费。许多重要的现实问题都涉及稀疏矩阵计算。由于这些问题的重要性，业界已开发出若干种稀疏矩阵存储格式及其相应的处理方法，并在该领域广泛使用。所有这些方法都采用某种压缩技术来避免存储或处理零元素，代价是在数据表示中引入某种程度的不规则性。遗憾的是，这种不规则性会导致并行计算中内存带宽利用不足、控制流分歧和负载不均衡。因此，在压缩与规则化之间取得良好平衡十分重要。有些存储格式以高度的不规则性为代价实现高度压缩；另一些则实现较适中的压缩，同时让表示更规则。已知使用每种存储格式的并行计算的相对性能，极大地依赖于稀疏矩阵中非零元素的分布。理解稀疏矩阵存储格式及其并行算法的丰富工作，能为并行程序员提供应对相关问题上压缩与规则化挑战的重要背景。

en: A graph is a data structure that represents the relations between entities. The entities involved are represented as vertices and the relations are represented as edges. Many important real-world problems are naturally formulated as large-scale graph problems and can benefit from massively parallel computation. Prominent examples include social networks and driving direction map services. There are multiple strategies for parallelizing graph computations, some of which are centered on processing vertices in parallel while others are centered on processing edges in parallel. Graphs are intrinsically related to sparse matrices because graph adjacency matrices tend to be very sparse. Graph computation can be formulated in terms of sparse matrix operations on square matrices. However, one can often improve the efficiency of graph computation by exploiting properties that are specific to the type of graph computation being performed. In this chapter, we will focus on breadth first search, a graph traversal computation that underlies many real-world applications.
zh: 图是一种表示实体之间关系的数据结构。所涉及的实体被表示为顶点，关系被表示为边。许多重要的现实问题可以自然地表述为大规模图问题，并能从大规模并行计算中受益。突出的例子包括社交网络和驾车路线地图服务。图计算并行化有多种策略，有的以并行处理顶点为中心，有的以并行处理边为中心。图与稀疏矩阵有内在联系，因为图的邻接矩阵往往非常稀疏；图计算可以用方阵上的稀疏矩阵运算来表述。然而，通过利用所执行的图计算类型特有的性质，人们往往可以提高图计算的效率。在本章中，我们将聚焦广度优先搜索——一种支撑许多现实应用的图遍历计算。

en: Deep learning [1] is a branch of the machine learning discipline whose studies give computers the ability to learn to perform certain tasks without being explicitly programmed. Machine learning for a task starts with a human developer architecting a parameterized model for given datasets that explicitly or implicitly specify the expected action for each input instance. The model parameters are “learned” by processing the datasets. The complexity and size of the machine learning models can vary widely based on the task being performed and the size of the datasets used. Deep learning models are designed for complex tasks, such as human facial recognition and natural language processing, whose expected actions can only be captured with and learned from datasets with massive numbers of examples. These models typically employ a deep hierarchy of classifiers that consist of a massive number of parameters to learn a large number of complex features. Thus, they can achieve more accurate pattern recognition results if there is enough training data to allow the system to properly learn the parameter values of all the layers of feature extractors in the model to automatically discover an adequate number of relevant patterns.

While machine learning has existed as a subject of computer science for a long time and has been applied successfully to automate many simple, routine tasks, its deep learning branch had stayed dormant for decades because of the lack of massive datasets and the computing power needed to learn the values of the large number of model parameters from the massive datasets. Since 2012, deep learning based on multi-layer Artificial Neural Networks has gained a great deal of industry attention for two reasons. The first reason is the massive datasets available for training deep learning models from the pervasive use of the internet by both consumers and businesses. The second reason is the availability of ample computing power in GPU computing systems that can effectively and timely learn model parameter values from these massive datasets. The readers may find the introduction to machine learning and neural networks in Appendix B helpful.

This chapter presents the acceleration of the convolutional neural networks (CNNs) whose demonstrated efficacy in computer vision triggered the first wave of deep learning revolution in 2012. In particular, the convolutional layers of the CNNs have a high compute-to-memory-access ratio, and high levels of parallelism, which makes them a perfect candidate for GPU acceleration. We will present a basic CUDA implementation of the forward (inference) path in a convolutional layer and a few optimizations that improve the speed of this basic implementation. We will then show how one can formulate the convolutional layers into matrix multiplication, which can be systematically accelerated using highly optimized hardware and software in modern GPUs.
zh: 深度学习[1]是机器学习学科的一个分支，其研究使计算机能够学会执行某些任务而无需被明确编程。针对一项任务的机器学习，始于人类开发者为给定数据集设计一个参数化模型；这些数据集显式或隐式地规定了每个输入实例的期望输出。模型参数通过处理数据集被“学习”出来。机器学习模型的复杂度和规模可大可小，取决于所执行的任务和所用数据集的大小。深度学习模型是为复杂任务设计的，例如人脸识别和自然语言处理，其期望输出只能用包含海量样本的数据集来刻画、并从中学习。这类模型通常采用由海量参数构成的深度分类器层级，以学习大量复杂特征。因此，若有足够的训练数据，使系统能够妥当学习模型中所有特征提取层的参数值、自动发现足够数量的相关模式，它们就能取得更精确的模式识别结果。

尽管机器学习作为计算机科学的一个课题早已存在，并被成功用于自动化许多简单的常规任务，但它的深度学习分支却一直沉寂了数十年，原因是缺少海量数据集，也缺少从海量数据集中学习大量模型参数值所需的算力。自 2012 年起，基于多层人工神经网络的深度学习因两个原因获得了产业界的极大关注。其一是消费者和企业对互联网的普遍使用，带来了可用于训练深度学习模型的海量数据集。其二是 GPU 计算系统提供了充足算力，能够高效、及时地从这些海量数据中学习模型参数值。读者可能觉得附录 B 对机器学习和神经网络的介绍会有帮助。
本章介绍卷积神经网络（CNN）的加速。CNN 在计算机视觉中展示的效力，引发了 2012 年第一波深度学习革命。特别地，CNN 的卷积层具有很高的计算访存比和很高的并行度，是 GPU 加速的理想对象。我们将给出卷积层前向（推理）路径的一个基本 CUDA 实现，以及若干提升该基本实现速度的优化；然后说明如何把卷积层表述为矩阵乘法，从而借助现代 GPU 中高度优化的硬件和软件得到系统性的加速。

en: Before Google Researchers introduced Transformers [1] in 2017, language tasks had been predominantly based on statistical language modeling techniques pioneered by IBM (e.g., [2]). In 2018, Google introduced the BERT language model based on Transformers and achieved unprecedented results in natural language tasks. Since then, the Transformer architecture has become the backbone of the deep learning approaches to natural language processing (NLP) based on neural networks.

Since then, LLMs have captured the attention of the industry and advanced rapidly, demonstrating human-level performance in diverse tasks such as text generation, summarization, translation, and conversation. These language models have grown by orders of magnitude in size compared to BERT to accommodate more training data. The term Large Language Models (LLMs) has been coined to distinguish them from previous generations of language models. While LLMs were originally developed to process and generate information in text form, multi-modal models (i.e., trained with and used for different types of visual, audio, and other types of data such as scientific data) started to appear.

The core idea of LLMs is to predict the next token (e.g., a word, sub-word, character) given a sequence of previous tokens. In chatbot applications such as ChatGPT [3], the sequence of previous tokens, collectively called the context, is composed of the system prompt, user input, and the tokens already generated by the model. In order for LLMs to generate accurate results, they contain billions of parameters (i.e., tens of layers with hundreds of millions of parameters each) that must be trained on huge datasets. During inference, large contexts help to provide more accurate responses. A mechanism, referred to as attention is needed to maintain the context and to identify the parts of the large context that are the most relevant to the generation of the next token. It is therefore important to understand the attention mechanism as well as the Transformer Architecture [1] which is the most popular approach to incorporating attention mechanisms into LLMs.
zh: 在 Google 的研究人员于 2017 年提出 Transformer[1] 之前，语言任务主要基于由 IBM 开创的统计语言建模技术（如[2]）。2018 年，Google 推出了基于 Transformer 的 BERT 语言模型，在自然语言任务上取得了前所未有的成绩。此后，Transformer 架构成为基于神经网络的自然语言处理（NLP）深度学习方法的骨干。

从那以后，大语言模型吸引了产业界的关注并快速演进，在文本生成、摘要、翻译、对话等多种任务上展现出与人类相当的水平。为容纳更多训练数据，这些语言模型的规模较 BERT 增长了数个数量级。“大语言模型”（Large Language Models，LLM）一词由此出现，用以将它们与前几代语言模型区分开来。虽然 LLM 最初是为处理和生成文本形式的信息而开发的，但多模态模型（即使用视觉、音频以及科学数据等其他类型的数据训练并用于处理的模型）也开始出现。

LLM 的核心思想是：给定前文 token（如词、子词、字符）序列，预测下一个 token。在 OpenAI ChatGPT[3] 这类聊天机器人应用中，前文 token 序列（统称上下文）由系统提示词、用户输入以及模型已经生成的 token 组成。为了让 LLM 生成准确的结果，模型包含数十亿参数（即数十层、每层数亿参数），且必须在海量数据集上训练。在推理阶段，大上下文有助于给出更准确的回答。这就需要注意（attention）机制来维护上下文，并在大上下文中识别与生成下一个 token 最相关的部分。因此，理解注意力机制以及把注意力机制融入 LLM 的最流行方案——Transformer 架构[1]——十分重要。（注：本章中“架构”一词指“神经网络架构”，而非本书其他部分所指的“硬件架构”。）

en: In this chapter, we use a molecular dynamics application based on regular grid data structures to illustrate the use of optimization techniques that achieve global memory access coalescing and improved computation throughput. We present a series of implementations of an electrostatic potential map calculation kernel, with each version improving upon the previous one. Each version adopts one or more practical techniques from Chapter 6. Some of the techniques are in common with the previous chapters but some are different: gather-to-scatter transformation, systematic reuse of computational results, and fast boundary condition checking. The effective use of these practical techniques can significantly improve application speed.
zh: 在本章中，我们用一个基于规则网格数据结构的分子动力学应用，来说明实现全局内存访问合并、提高计算吞吐量的优化技术的使用。我们给出静电网格势图计算内核的一系列实现，每一版本都在上一版本的基础上有所改进。每个版本都采用了第 6 章中的一种或多种实用技术。其中一些技术与前面各章常见，另一些则不同：gather 到 scatter 的变换、计算结果的系统性复用，以及快速边界条件检查。有效运用这些实用技术，可以显著提升应用速度。

en: We have so far concentrated on practical knowledge in parallel programming, which consists of CUDA programming features, the GPU architecture, performance optimization techniques, parallel patterns, and application case studies. In this chapter, we switch our discussions to concepts that are more abstract. We first generalize parallel programming into a thinking process of designing/selecting parallel algorithms and decomposing a domain problem into well-defined and coordinated parallel work units that can each be efficiently performed by the selected algorithms. With good algorithm selection and problem decomposition, the programmer can achieve an appropriate compromise between parallelism, work efficiency, and resource consumption.

A strong combination of domain knowledge and parallel thinking skills is often needed for creating successful computational solutions to challenging domain problems. With strong parallel thinking skills, a parallel programmer does not need to be confined to the role of solving domain problems handed down by domain scientists. Rather, the programmer can collaborate with domain scientists to analyze and transform the structure of a domain problem: which parts are inherently serial, which parts are amenable to high-performance parallel execution, and the domain-specific tradeoffs involved in moving parts from the former category to the latter. This chapter gives the reader more insight into parallel programming and parallel thinking in general.
zh: 到目前为止，我们专注于并行编程的实践知识，包括 CUDA 编程特性、GPU 架构、性能优化技术、并行模式和应用案例研究。在本章中，我们把讨论转向更抽象的概念。我们首先把并行编程概括为一个思维过程：设计/选择并行算法，并把领域问题分解为定义良好、彼此协调、可由所选算法各自高效执行的并行工作单元。有了良好的算法选择和问题分解，程序员就能在并行度、工作效率和资源消耗之间取得恰当的折中。
要为困难的领域问题创造出成功的计算解决方案，往往需要领域知识与并行思维技能的强大结合。有了很强的并行思维技能，并行程序员就不必把自己局限为解决领域科学家交下来的领域问题的角色。恰恰相反，程序员可以与领域科学家协作，分析和转变领域问题的结构：哪些部分是本质上顺序的，哪些部分适合高性能并行执行，以及把部分从前者移到后者所涉及的领域特定权衡。本章帮助读者对并行编程与一般的并行思维获得更多洞察。

en: So far, we have focused on programming a heterogeneous computing system with one host and one device. However, many applications require the aggregate computing power of multiple hosts and devices. Many clusters and data centers today have one or more hosts and one or more devices attached to each host. In this chapter, we look at three programming models for programming clusters with multiple GPUs: the Message Passing Interface (MPI) [1], the NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) [2], and the NVIDIA OpenSHMEM Library (NVSHMEM) [3]. We only present the key concepts from each programming model that a programmer needs to understand in order to scale their heterogeneous applications to multiple GPUs and nodes in a cluster environment. We focus on domain partitioning, point-to-point communication, collective communication, and overlapping computation and communication in the context of scaling a CUDA stencil computation across multiple GPU nodes. The implementations presented are intended to illustrate the core principles behind each programming model and can each be further optimized within their respective programming models. Readers are encouraged to refer to tutorials and application case studies of each of the three programming models for a more extensive coverage of the full capabilities of each model once they master the concepts in this chapter.
zh: 到目前为止，我们专注于对一个主机和一个设备组成的异构计算系统编程。然而，许多应用需要多台主机和多台设备的算力总和。如今的许多集群和数据中心都有一台或多台主机，每台主机又连接着一台或多台设备。在本章中，我们研究三种面向多 GPU 集群的编程模型：消息传递接口（MPI）[1]、NVIDIA 集合通信库（NCCL）[2] 和 NVIDIA OpenSHMEM 库（NVSHMEM）[3]。我们只介绍每种编程模型中程序员需要理解的关键概念，以把其异构应用扩展到集群环境中的多个 GPU 和节点。我们聚焦域划分、点对点通信、集合通信以及计算与通信的重叠，背景是把 CUDA 模板计算扩展到多个 GPU 节点。所给出的实现旨在说明每种编程模型背后的核心原理，并且各自都可以在相应的编程模型内进一步优化。希望读者在掌握本章概念后，参考这三种编程模型的教程和应用案例研究，更全面地了解每个模型的全部能力。

en: You made it! We have arrived at the finishing line. In this final chapter, we will briefly review the learning goals that you have achieved through this book. Instead of drawing a conclusion, we will offer our vision for the future of massively parallel computing and how its advancements will impact the future course of science and technology.
zh: 你做到了！我们已经抵达终点线。在这最后一章，我们将简要回顾你通过本书实现的学习目标。我们不作结论，而是分享我们对大规模并行计算未来的展望，以及它的进步将如何影响科学与技术的未来走向。

en: In the early days of computing, floating-point arithmetic capability was found only in mainframes and supercomputers. Although many microprocessors designed in the 1980’s started to have floating-point coprocessors, their floating-point arithmetic speed was extremely slow, about three orders of magnitude slower than that of mainframes and supercomputers. With advances in microprocessor technology, many microprocessors designed in the 1990’s, such as Intel Pentium III and AMD Athlon, started to have high performance floating-point capabilities that rival supercomputers. High speed floating-point arithmetic has become a standard feature for microprocessors and GPUs today. More recently, in response to the unsatisfiable demand for high-speed floating-point arithmetic from LLM training and inference use cases, GPUs have dramatically increased the throughput of their floating-point throughput. Floating-point representation allows for larger dynamic range of representable data values and more precise representation of tiny data values than its integer counterpart. These desirable properties make floating-point preferred data representative for modeling the physical and artificial phenomena, such as combustion, aerodynamics, light illumination, and financial risks [1]. Large scale evaluation of these models has been driving the need for parallel computing. As a result, it is important for application programmers to understand the nature of floating-point arithmetic in developing their parallel applications. In particular, we will focus on the accuracy of floating-point arithmetic operations, the precision of floating-point number representation, the stability of numerical algorithms and how they should be taken into consideration in parallel programming.
zh: 在计算的早期年代，只有大型机和超级计算机才具备浮点运算能力。尽管 20 世纪 80 年代设计的许多微处理器开始配备浮点协处理器，但它们的浮点运算速度极慢，比大型机和超级计算机慢约三个数量级。随着微处理器技术的进步，20 世纪 90 年代设计的许多微处理器，例如 Intel Pentium III 和 AMD Athlon，开始拥有可与超级计算机媲美的高性能浮点能力。如今，高速浮点运算已经成为微处理器和 GPU 的标准特性。最近些年，为回应大语言模型训练与推理场景对高速浮点运算的无止境需求，GPU 大幅提升了其浮点吞吐量。与整数表示相比，浮点表示允许表示更大动态范围的数据值，也能更精确地表示极小的数据值。这些理想的特性，使浮点成为对燃烧、空气动力学、光照、金融风险等物理与人造现象建模时的首选数据表示[1]。对这些模型的大规模评估，一直在驱动对并行计算的需求。因此，应用程序员在开发并行应用时理解浮点运算的本质十分重要。具体而言，我们将关注浮点算术运算的准确性（accuracy）、浮点数表示的精度（precision）、数值算法的稳定性（stability），以及它们在并行编程中应如何被考虑。

en: Machine learning, a term coined by Arthur Samuel of IBM in 1959 [1], is a field of computer science which studies methods for learning application logic from data rather than designing explicit algorithms. Machine learning is most successful in computing tasks where designing explicit algorithms is infeasible, mostly because there is not enough knowledge in the design of such explicit algorithms. That is, one can give examples on what should happen in various situations but not general rules for making such decisions for all possible inputs. For example, machine learning has contributed to the recent improvements in application areas such as automatic speech recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, and recommender systems. In these application areas, one can provide many input examples and what should come out for each input, but there is no algorithm that can correctly process all possible inputs.

The kinds of application logic created with machine learning can be organized according to the types of tasks that they perform. There is a wide range of machine learning tasks. Here we show a few out of a large number:

- Classification -- to determine to which of the k categories an input belongs. An example is object recognition: which type of food is shown in this photo?
- Regression -- to predict a numerical value given some inputs. An example is to predict the price of a stock at the end of the next trading day.
- Transcription -- to convert unstructured data into textual form. An example is optical character recognition.
- Translation -- to convert a sequence of symbols in one language to a sequence of symbols in another. An example is translating from English to Chinese.
- Embedding -- to convert an input to a vector while preserving relationships between entities. An example is to convert a natural language sentence into a multi-dimensional vector.

The readers are referred to a large body of literature on the mathematical background and practical solutions to the various tasks of machine learning. The purpose of this appendix is to introduce the computation kernels involved in the neural network approach to the classification task. A concrete understanding of these kernels will allow the reader to understand and develop kernels for deep learning approaches to other machine learning tasks. As such, in the next section, we will go into details of the classification task to establish the background knowledge needed to understand neural networks.
zh: 机器学习（machine learning）是 IBM 的 Arthur Samuel 于 1959 年创造的术语[1]，它是计算机科学的一个领域，研究从数据中学习应用逻辑的方法，而不是设计显式的算法。机器学习最成功之处，在于那些设计显式算法不可行的计算任务——往往是因为在设计这类显式算法时知识不足：也就是说，人们可以给出在各种情况下应当发生什么的例子，却给不出能为所有可能输入做出这些决策的一般规则。例如，机器学习促成了自动语音识别、计算机视觉、自然语言处理和推荐系统等应用领域近年来的进步。在这些应用领域中，人们可以提供许多输入示例以及每个输入应有的输出，却不存在能正确处理所有可能输入的算法。

用机器学习创建的应用逻辑可以按其所执行任务的类型组织。机器学习任务的范围很广，这里只从大量任务中列举几个：

- 分类（Classification）——判定输入属于 k 个类别中的哪一个。例子是目标识别：这张照片展示的是哪类食物？
- 回归（Regression）——给定若干输入，预测一个数值。例子是预测某只股票在下一个交易日结束时的价格。
- 转录（Transcription）——把非结构化数据转换为文本形式。例子是光学字符识别。
- 翻译（Translation）——把一种语言的符号序列转换为另一种语言的符号序列。例子是把英文翻译成中文。
- 嵌入（Embedding）——把输入转换为向量，同时保留实体之间的关系。例子是把一个自然语言句子转换为多维向量。
关于机器学习各类任务的数学背景和实际解决方案，请读者参阅大量文献。本附录的目的是介绍分类任务的神经网络方法所涉及的计算内核。对这些内核有具体理解后，读者就能理解并开发面向其他机器学习任务的深度学习方法的内核。因此，在下一节中，我们将深入讨论分类任务的细节，为理解神经网络建立背景知识。

en: Throughout this book, we have mostly assumed a fairly simple model of interaction between the host and the device in a heterogeneous computing system. In this simple model, as presented in Chapter 2, each device has a device memory (CUDA global memory) that is separate from the host memory, or the system memory. The data to be processed by a kernel running on a device need to be transferred from the host memory to the device memory by calling the cudaMemcpy() function. The data produced by the device also need to be transferred from the device memory to the host by calling the cudaMemcpy() function before it can be utilized by the host. Early GPU generations only supported this simple host/device interaction model. Although the model is simple and easy to understand, it has resulted in several problems at the application level.

First, I/O devices such as disk controllers and network interface cards are designed to operate efficiently on the host memory. Since the device memory is separate from the host memory, input data need to be transferred from the host memory to the device memory and output data need to be transferred from the device memory to the host memory for use by I/O devices. Such additional transfers increase the I/O latency and reduce the achievable I/O throughput. For many applications, the ability of I/O devices to operate directly on the device memory would improve overall application performance and simplify the application code.

Second, traditional programming systems such as Python place their application data structures in the host memory. Some of the data structures are large. The device memory in CUDA-enabled GPUs tends to offer higher bandwidth but smaller capacity compared to the host memory, which forces application developers to partition their large data structures into chunks that each fit into the device memory. For example, in Chapter 21, the 3D electrostatic energy grid array was partitioned into 2D slices that are transferred between the host memory and the device memory. For many applications, it would be much better if entire data structures can reside in the device memory. For some applications, there may not even be a good way to partition the data structure into smaller chunks. For these applications, it would be best if the GPU can directly access the data in the host memory or have the CUDA runtime system software to migrate the data that are used during kernel execution.

As more applications adopted GPU computing, their needs motivated CUDA system software developers and GPU hardware designers to provide a better solution. Researchers have been aware of these needs and have proposed solutions since the early days of CUDA [1]. The rest of this section will go over a brief history of advancements that address these limitations.
zh: 在本书中，我们几乎一直假设异构计算系统中主机与设备之间的交互是一个相当简单的模型。在这个第 2 章介绍的简单模型中，每个设备都有一块与主机内存（系统内存）分离的设备内存（CUDA 全局内存）。设备上运行的内核要处理的数据，需要先调用 cudaMemcpy() 函数从主机内存传送到设备内存；设备产生的数据，也需要调用 cudaMemcpy() 函数从设备内存传回主机，才能被主机使用。早期几代 GPU 只支持这种简单的主机/设备交互模型。这个模型虽然简单易懂，却在应用层面带来了若干问题。
第一，磁盘控制器、网卡等 I/O 设备是按高效地针对主机内存工作来设计的。由于设备内存与主机内存分离，输入数据要先从主机内存传到设备内存、输出数据要从设备内存传回主机内存，才能供 I/O 设备使用。这些额外的传输增加了 I/O 延迟，降低了可达到的 I/O 吞吐量。对许多应用而言，若 I/O 设备能直接对设备内存进行操作，将提升整体应用性能并简化应用代码。

第二，传统编程系统（如 Python）把应用的数据结构放在主机内存中，其中一些数据结构非常大。支持 CUDA 的 GPU 的设备内存往往比主机内存带宽更高但容量更小，这迫使应用开发者把大数据结构划分成每个都能放进设备内存的块。例如在第 21 章中，三维静电势能网格数组被划分为二维切片，在主机内存与设备内存之间来回传输。对许多应用来说，如果整个数据结构都能驻留在设备内存中会好得多。对某些应用，甚至可能找不到把数据结构划分成较小块的好办法。对这些应用而言，最好的办法是 GPU 能直接访问主机内存中的数据，或者由 CUDA 运行时系统软件迁移内核执行期间使用的数据。
随着越来越多的应用采用 GPU 计算，它们的需求促使 CUDA 系统软件开发人员和 GPU 硬件设计者提供更好的解决方案。研究人员从 CUDA 早期就意识到这些需求并提出了方案[1]。本节其余部分将简要回顾解决这些限制的技术进展历史。
